Shares of Nvidia and Micron Technology are set to rise Friday morning after OpenAI told investors it expects its annualized revenue to reach or exceed $70 billion by the end of 2026, according to Bloomberg. The projection follows a day of selling in chip stocks tied to the AI buildout. The company declined to comment to Bloomberg. Shares of Nvidia, Oracle, and CoreWeave fell Thursday, and the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.4%, after OpenAI's annualized revenue figure of approximately $50 billion as of late September became public — a number that fell short of the widely cited $68 billion figure that had been circulating among investors. The $68 billion figure had originated from investors applying Anthropic's methodology to OpenAI's numbers, which then fed into reports citing figures of roughly $68 billion to $70 billion. OpenAI is seeking to raise around $30 billion in a new funding round, with no term sheet finalized, according to Bloomberg.

highlights: Nvidia GPUs are the most sought-after processors in AI, and they're in such demand that the chipmaker's stock climbed to yet another record this week, lifting its market cap close to $6 trillion. Customers can now shop around for access to the chips at the giant clouds from Amazon, Microsoft and Google, as well as at so-called neoclouds like CoreWeave. For Nvidia, it all adds up to unrelenting growth, as management anticipates $108 billion in revenue for the October quarter, which would mark an 89% year-over-year jump. While cloud infrastructure providers have ranked at the top of Nvidia's customer list for several years, the business is diversifying. "Some of the hyperscalers have approached us about taking care of customers they're worried about because they don't have the ability to service those customers when they need it," said Marc Boroditsky, chief revenue officer of Nebius, a Netherlands-based neocloud with operations in the U.S. Video generation startup Reactor uses GPUs through Nebius and hyperscalers, said CEO Alberto Taiuti.
